<!-- rem-1: body_md -->
\label{rhf97hf93h8f9j3fj0}
Note that $\wedge^\bullet \mathcal{E}$ is a sheaf of $\mathbb{Z}_2$-graded, supercommutative algebras. It also admits a compatible $\mathbb{Z}$-grading. We will however only consider automorphisms of $\wedge^\bullet \mathcal{E}$ which preserve the $\mathbb{Z}_2$-grading. The sheaf of such automorphisms will be denoted $\operatorname{{\mathcal A}ut}_{\mathbb{Z}_2}(\wedge^\bullet \mathcal{E})$. However we will suppress the subscript `$\mathbb{Z}_2$' so as to avoid cumbersome notation and simply write $\operatorname{{\mathcal A}ut}\wedge^\bullet \mathcal{E}$.
<!-- end rem-1 -->
<!-- def-1: body_md -->
\label{rfh89hf98hf8030}A \emph{supermanifold modelled on $(X, E)$} is an element of the \v{C}ech cohomology set $\check{H}^1\big(X, \mathcal{G}_{(X, E)}^{(2)}\big)$.
<!-- end def-1 -->
<!-- def-2: body_md -->
\label{rhrhf8938fj30fj03}
The basepoint in $\check{H}^1\big(X, \mathcal{G}_{(X, E)}^{(2)}\big)$ is referred to as \emph{the split supermanifold} model\-led on~$(X, E)$, or simply the \emph{split model}.
<!-- end def-2 -->
<!-- thm-1: body_md -->
\label{groeiveytvdbno}
Let $X$ be a $($paracompact$)$ topological space and suppose the following is a short exact sequence of sheaves of $($not necessarily abelian$)$ groups on~$X$
\begin{gather*}
e\longrightarrow A\longrightarrow B\longrightarrow C\longrightarrow e.
\end{gather*}
Then there exists a long exact sequence
\begin{align}
e & \longrightarrow H^0(X, A) \longrightarrow H^0(X, B) \longrightarrow H^0(X, C)\label{rhf894h98ffj093j03}\\
&\longrightarrow \check{H}^1(X, A) \longrightarrow\check{H}^1(X, B)\longrightarrow\check{H}^1(X, C),\label{kfjvbtbrnnvoir}
\end{align}
where the sequence in \eqref{rhf894h98ffj093j03} is as groups whereas that in \eqref{kfjvbtbrnnvoir} is as pointed sets. Furthermore, there exists an action of $H^0(X, C)$ on the set $\check{H}^1(X, A)$ such that the following diagram commutes
\begin{gather*}
\xymatrix{\ar[dr]\check{H}^1(X, A) \ar[rr] & & \check{H}^1(X, B)\\
& \check{H}^1(X, A)/H^0(X, C).\ar@{-->}[ur]&}
\end{gather*}
<!-- end thm-1 -->
<!-- def-3: body_md -->
\label{rfhhf983fj390f3}Two supermanifolds modelled on $(X, E)$ are \emph{isomorphic} if and only if their image in $\check{H}^1\big(X, \operatorname{{\mathcal A}ut}\wedge^\bullet\mathcal{E}\big)$ coincide.
<!-- end def-3 -->
<!-- thm-2: body_md -->
\label{rh9r8h984hf89jf0fj3}There exists a bijective correspondence
\begin{gather*}
\frac{\left\{\text{\rm supermanifolds modelled on $(X, E)$}\right\}}{\text{\rm up to isomorphism}} \cong \frac{\check{H}^1\big(X, \mathcal{G}^{(2)}_{(X, E)}\big)}{\operatorname{Aut}(E)}.
\end{gather*}
<!-- end thm-2 -->
<!-- def-4: body_md -->
A supermanifold if said to be \emph{split} if and only if it is isomorphic to the split model.
<!-- end def-4 -->
<!-- que-1: body_md -->
\label{rfiufh498fj894fj0409}Given a supermanifold, how can one tell if it is split?
<!-- end que-1 -->
<!-- prop-1: body_md -->
\label{rjf984jf894jf90f903k0}
For each $k\geq 2$ there exists a short exact sequence of sheaves of groups
\begin{gather*}
\{e\} \longrightarrow \mathcal{G}^{(k+1)}_{(X, E)} \longrightarrow \mathcal{G}^{(k)}_{(X, E)} \longrightarrow \mathcal{Q}^{(k)}_{(X, E)} \longrightarrow \{e\},
\end{gather*}
where the inclusion $\mathcal{G}^{(k+1)}_{(X, E)} \rightarrow \mathcal{G}^{(k)}_{(X, E)}$ is normal and the factor $\mathcal{Q}^{(k)}_{(X, E)}$ is abelian.
<!-- end prop-1 -->
<!-- def-5: body_md -->
\label{rhf94h98h489fj90fk903k}To any model $(X, E)$ we term the following important constructs for each $k\geq 2$:
\begin{itemize}\itemsep=0pt
	\item the sheaf $\mathcal{Q}^{(k)}_{(X, E)}$ in Proposition~\ref{rjf984jf894jf90f903k0} is referred to as the $k$-th \emph{obstruction sheaf};
	\item the cohomology group $H^1\big(X, \mathcal{Q}_{(X, E)}^{(k)}\big)$ is referred to as the \emph{$k$-th obstruction space}.
\end{itemize}
<!-- end def-5 -->
<!-- def-6: body_md -->
\label{rjfi4fj04kf0kf03kf3}
Let $\mathfrak{X}$ be a supermanifold modelled on $(X, E)$. The class $\omega_*(\mathfrak{X})$ in the second obstruction space will be referred to as the \emph{primary obstruction} to splitting $\mathfrak{X}$.
<!-- end def-6 -->
<!-- thm-3: body_md -->
\label{4fh984fj8jf093j303kf}Let $\mathfrak{X}$ be a supermanifold. If its primary obstruction is non-vanishing, then $\mathfrak{X}$ is non-split.
<!-- end thm-3 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
proof of this theorem, stated using the notion of `retractibility,' can be found in \cite[Theorem 4.6.2, p.~158]{BER}. For completeness, we present a proof based on our formulation of isomorphisms of supermanifolds in Definition \ref{rfhhf983fj390f3}. As the proof is a little involved, we defer it to Appendix~\ref{rgf784g87hf98j3fj0j9f33}.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- def-7: body_md -->
An element in $\check{H}^1\big(X, \mathcal{G}^{(k)}_{(X, E)}\big)$ is referred to as a \emph{$(k-1)$-split atlas} for a supermanifold modelled on $(X, E)$.
<!-- end def-7 -->
<!-- def-8: body_md -->
\label{hf894f894jfj09f30}If a supermanifold $\mathfrak{X}$ lies in the image of a $(k-1)$-split atlas $\mathfrak{X}^{(k)}$, then $\mathfrak{X}$ is said to be \emph{$(k-1)$-split}. Conversely, the image of $\mathfrak{X}^{(k)}$ in $\check{H}^1\big(X, \mathcal{G}^{(2)}_{(X, E)}\big)$ will be referred to as the \emph{supermanifold associated to $\mathfrak{X}^{(k)}$}.
<!-- end def-8 -->
<!-- def-9: body_md -->
\label{rfh479f74hf893jf038jf93} The class in the $k$-th obstruction space associated to any $(k-1)$-split atlas will be referred to as the \emph{primary obstruction of the $(k-1)$-split atlas}.
<!-- end def-9 -->
<!-- def-10: body_md -->
If the primary obstruction of a $(k-1)$-split atlas $\mathfrak{X}^{(k)}$ is non-vanishing, then~$\mathfrak{X}^{(k)}$ is said to be \emph{obstructed}.
<!-- end def-10 -->
<!-- thm-4: body_md -->
\label{rh94hf94hf984jf9j093}A supermanifold $\mathfrak{X}$ is split if and only if it admits a $(k-1)$-split atlas for $k> q$.
<!-- end thm-4 -->
<!-- def-11: body_md -->
\label{rfh974hf9h389fj3}A $(k-1)$-split atlas $\mathfrak{X}^{(k)}$, $k>2$, is said to be \emph{weakly non-split} if its associated supermanifold does not coincide with the basepoint. Otherwise, it is said to be \emph{strongly split}. We say $\mathfrak{X}^{(k)}$ is split or non-split if its associated supermanifold is split or non-split.
<!-- end def-11 -->
<!-- que-2: body_md -->
\label{rfh89hf98j3f09j039f3}When will a given $(k-1)$-split atlas be weakly non-split?
<!-- end que-2 -->
<!-- def-12: body_md -->
\label{rfn4ufh4f8jf039j903jrrr}
A $(k-1)$-split atlas $\mathfrak{X}^{(k)}$, for $k> 2$, is said to be \emph{exotic} if it entertains the following two properties:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]\itemsep=0pt
	\item $\mathfrak{X}^{(k)}$ is obstructed;
	\item $\mathfrak{X}^{(k)}$ is strongly split.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end def-12 -->
<!-- lem-1: body_md -->
\label{4hf84hf89hf8998f3j}Let $\mathfrak{X}^{(k)}$ be an obstructed, $(k-1)$-split atlas for $k>2$. If there exists a non-zero $\phi\in H^0\big(X, \mathcal{Q}^{(k-1)}_{(X, E)}\big)$ such that $\alpha(\phi) = \mathfrak{X}^{(k)}$, then $\mathfrak{X}^{(k)}$ will be exotic.
<!-- end lem-1 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Let $\mathfrak{X}^{(k)}$ be a $(k-1)$-split atlas and suppose $\alpha(\phi) = \mathfrak{X}^{(k)}$, for some non-zero $\phi\in H^0\big(X, \mathcal{Q}^{(k-1)}_{(X, E)}\big)$. In assuming $\mathfrak{X}^{(k)}$ is obstructed, it cannot represent the basepoint in $\check{H}^1\big(X, \mathcal{G}^{(k)}_{(X, E)}\big)$. Now by exactness of the sequence in \eqref{fnvrvknencoeioie}--\eqref{rh47fh984f09fj903ff} note, under $\beta$, that $\mathfrak{X}^{(k)}$ will map to the basepoint in $\check{H}^1\big(X, \mathcal{G}^{(k-1)}_{(X, E)}\big)$. Hence it will map to the basepoint in $\check{H}^1\big(X, \mathcal{G}^{(2)}_{(X, E)}\big)$. Thus $\mathfrak{X}^{(k)}$ is obstructed and strongly split. Hence $\mathfrak{X}^{(k)}$ is exotic.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- prop-2: body_md -->
\label{tyhryg7hfiujfoiej}
Suppose that $H^0\big(X, \mathcal{Q}^{(k)}_{(X, E)}\big) = (0)$ for all $k>2$. Then there do not exist exotic atlases for any supermanifold modelled on~$(X, E)$.
<!-- end prop-2 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
uppose $H^0\big(X, \mathcal{Q}_{(X, E)}^{(k)}\big) = (0)$. Then from \eqref{fnvrvknencoeioie} we have the exact sequence of pointed sets
\begin{gather}
\{e\} \longrightarrow \check{H}^1\big(X, \mathcal{G}_{(X, E)}^{(k+1)}\big) \stackrel{\iota_*^{k+1}}{\longrightarrow} \check{H}^1\big(X, \mathcal{G}_{(X, E)}^{(k)}\big).\label{rhf794hf89hf03j93}
\end{gather}
Unlike for rings or modules, an exact sequence as in \eqref{rhf794hf89hf03j93} above need not imply $\iota_*^{k+1}$ will be injective as a map of sets. But for $\mathfrak{X}^{(k+1)}\in \check{H}^1\big(X, \mathcal{G}_{(X, E)}^{(k+1)}\big)$ we can nevertheless conclude the following implication from exactness of \eqref{rhf794hf89hf03j93}:
\begin{gather}
\big(\iota_*^{k+1}\big(\mathfrak{X}^{(k+1)}\big) = \{e\}\big) \Longrightarrow \big(\mathfrak{X}^{(k+1)} = \{e\}\big).\label{fh784hfhf983jfj30}
\end{gather}
Assume now that $H^0\big(X, \mathcal{Q}_{(X, E)}^{(k)}\big) =(0)$ for all $k$. Then the implication~\eqref{fh784hfhf983jfj30} will hold for all $k$. Let $\mathfrak{X}^{(k+1)}\in \check{H}^1\big(X, \mathcal{G}_{(X, E)}^{(k+1)}\big)$ and suppose it maps to the basepoint in $ \check{H}^1\big(X, \mathcal{G}_{(X, E)}^{(2)}\big)$. It will then follow from~\eqref{fh784hfhf983jfj30} that $\mathfrak{X}^{(k+1)}= \{e\}$. Hence~$\mathfrak{X}^{(k+1)}$ cannot be obstructed and so, by definition, cannot be exotic.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- rem-2: body_md -->
\label{rhf984hf89hf893h8}For $E\rightarrow X$ a holomorphic, rank $q$ vector bundle it is superfluous to assume $H^0\big(X, \mathcal{Q}^{(q)}_{(X, E)}\big) = (0)$ in Proposition~\ref{tyhryg7hfiujfoiej}. This is because $\mathcal{G}^{(k)}_{(X, E)} = \{e\}$ for all $k> q$, meaning we already have $\{e\}\rightarrow\check{H}^1\big(X, \mathcal{G}^{(q)}_{(X, E)}\big)
\rightarrow \check{H}^1\big(X, \mathcal{G}^{(q-1)}_{(X, E)}\big)$. That is, Proposition~\ref{tyhryg7hfiujfoiej} will be valid under the slightly weakened assumption that $H^0\big(X, \mathcal{Q}^{(k)}_{(X, E)}\big) = (0)$ for all $2 < k < q$.
<!-- end rem-2 -->
<!-- def-13: body_md -->
\label{rh89hf89jf093j9f0fj03}A model $(X, E)$ is said to be \emph{good} if there do not exist any exotic atlases for any supermanifold modelled on $(X, E)$. Otherwise, it is said to support exotic atlases.
<!-- end def-13 -->
<!-- lem-2: body_md -->
\label{futhirhhiofoirjfoi}Let $(X, E)$ be a good model. Then if a $(k-1)$-split atlas modelled on $(X, E)$ is obstructed, it will be weakly non-split.
<!-- end lem-2 -->
<!-- thm-5: body_md -->
\label{ruihf8h98f983jfj30f}
A model $(X, E)$ will be a good if and only if taking global sections preserves exactness of the sequence
\begin{gather*}
\{e\}\longrightarrow \mathcal{G}^{(k+1)}_{(X, E)} \longrightarrow \mathcal{G}^{(k)}_{(X, E)} \longrightarrow \mathcal{Q}^{(k)}_{(X, E)}\longrightarrow \{e\}
\end{gather*}
for all $k\geq 2$.
<!-- end thm-5 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
rom the exact sequence of sheaves of groups $\mathcal{G}^{(k+1)}_{(X, E)} \rightarrow \mathcal{G}^{(k)}_{(X, E)} \rightarrow \mathcal{Q}^{(k)}_{(X, E)}$ we have the following piece of the long exact sequence on cohomology
\begin{align}
\{e\}& \longrightarrow H^0\big(X, \mathcal{G}^{(k+1)}_{(X, E)}\big) \longrightarrow H^0\big(X, \mathcal{G}^{(k)}_{(X, E)}\big) \longrightarrow H^0\big(X, \mathcal{Q}^{(k)}_{(X, E)}\big)\nonumber\\
&\stackrel{\alpha}{\longrightarrow} \check{H}^1\big(X, \mathcal{G}^{(k+1)}_{(X, E)}\big) \longrightarrow \cdots.\label{tuirguhf74hf84fjo}
\end{align}
In the direction $(\Leftarrow)$ in the statement of this theorem, assume~\eqref{tuirguhf74hf84fjo} is exact for all $k\geq 2$. Then either $H^0\big(X, \mathcal{Q}^{(k)}_{(X, E)}\big) = (0)$ for all $k\geq 2$ or the map $\alpha$ is constant, sending every $\phi \in H^0\big(X, \mathcal{Q}^{(k-1)}_{(X, E)}\big)$ to the basepoint~$\{e\}$. In either case, the proof of Proposition~\ref{tyhryg7hfiujfoiej} will apply since we will obtain exact sequences in \eqref{rhf794hf89hf03j93} for all $k$. In the direction $(\Rightarrow)$, suppose $(X, E)$ is a good model. We will show that $\alpha$ is constant. Firstly, by definition we know that there will not exist any exotic atlases. Therefore, for any $\phi\in H^0\big(X, \mathcal{Q}_{(X, E)}^{(k)}\big)$, the atlas~$\alpha(\phi)$ must be an unobstructed, $k$-split atlas, for otherwise it would be exotic by Lemma~\ref{4hf84hf89hf8998f3j}. Observe that as a~result we have the following lifting~$\widetilde\alpha$ of $\alpha$, represented by the dashed arrow
\begin{gather}\begin{split}&
\xymatrix{
& \check{H}^1\big(X, \mathcal{G}^{(k+2)}_{(X, E)}\big)\ar[d]\ar[dr]
\\
H^0\big(X, \mathcal{Q}_{(X, E)}^{(k)}\big)\ar@{-->}[ur]^{\widetilde\alpha}
\ar[r]^\alpha & \check{H}^1\big(X, \mathcal{G}^{(k+1)}_{(X, E)}\big)
\ar[d]^{\omega_*}
\ar[r] & \check{H}^1\big(X, \mathcal{G}^{(k)}_{(X, E)}\big)
\\
& H^1\big(X, \mathcal{Q}^{(k+1)}_{(X, E)}\big).
}\end{split}\label{rj984h98f8jj903jf903}
\end{gather}
The lifting $\widetilde\alpha$ exists since the vertical maps in \eqref{rj984h98f8jj903jf903} are exact and unobstructedness of $\alpha(\phi)$ means $\omega_*\big(\alpha(\phi)\big) = 0$. Hence from $\phi$ we obtain a $(k+1)$-split atlas $\widetilde \alpha(\phi)$. We claim that~$\widetilde\alpha(\phi)$ is also unobstructed. To see this note that~\eqref{rj984h98f8jj903jf903} will commute and so $\widetilde\alpha(\phi)$ will map to the basepoint in $\check{H}^1\big(X, \mathcal{G}^{(k)}_{(X, E)}\big)$. As such it will map to the basepoint in $\check{H}^1\big(X, \mathcal{G}^{(2)}_{(X, E)}\big)$ and so be split. This means, if $\widetilde\alpha(\phi)$ were obstructed, it would be exotic, contradicting that~$(X, E)$ is a~good model. Hence $\widetilde\alpha(\phi)$ must be unobstructed. Applying this argument again to $\widetilde\alpha(\phi)$ will show that $\widetilde\alpha$ will itself lift to some $\widetilde\alpha^\prime$ valued in $\check{H}^1\big(X, \mathcal{G}^{(k+3)}_{(X, E)}\big)$ and that to $\phi$ will be associated an unobstructed, $(k+2)$-split atlas. We can proceed inductively now and keep lifting the map~$\alpha$ to get unobstructed, $k^\prime$-split atlases for any $k^\prime> k$, resulting in the commutative diagram
\begin{gather}\begin{split}&
\xymatrix{
& \check{H}^1\big(X, \mathcal{G}^{(k^\prime)}_{(X, E)}\big)\ar[d]
\\
H^0\big(X, \mathcal{Q}_{(X, E)}^{(k)}\big)\ar@{-->}[ur]^{\widetilde\alpha^{k^\prime}}
\ar[r]^\alpha & \check{H}^1\big(X, \mathcal{G}^{(k+1)}_{(X, E)}\big).
}\end{split}\label{rfh49fh948fj984jf0}
\end{gather}
Since $\mathcal{G}^{(k^\prime)}_{(X, E)}$ is trivial for $k^\prime$ sufficiently large, commutativity of~\eqref{rfh49fh948fj984jf0} requires~$\alpha$ map~$\phi$ to the basepoint~$\{e\}$ for all~$\phi$. Thus~$\alpha$ is constant. This argument is independent of $k\geq 2$ and depends only on $(X, E)$ being a good model. The theorem now follows.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- rem-3: body_md -->
Concerning the diagram \eqref{rj984h98f8jj903jf903}, it is argued in \cite[Theorem~4.7.1, pp.~163--164]{BER} and in~\cite[p.~16]{DW1} that there will always exist a lift $\widetilde\alpha$ of $\alpha$ when $k$ is odd.
<!-- end rem-3 -->
<!-- lem-3: body_md -->
\label{fufh48hf89j4f09j09f3p}To any model $(X, E)$ there exists an isomorphism of sheaves
\begin{gather}
\mathcal{Q}^{(k)}_{(X, E)}=
\begin{cases}
\wedge^k\mathcal{E}\otimes T_X, & \text{$k$ is even},\\
\mathcal{E}^*\otimes \wedge^k\mathcal{E}, & \text{$k$ is odd}.
\end{cases}\label{rjf9804jf93jf903jf093j03}
\end{gather}
<!-- end lem-3 -->
<!-- prop-3: body_md -->
\label{rhf4hf84hf89jf893}Let $X$ be a Riemann surface of genus $g$ and $E\rightarrow X$ a rank $3$, holomorphic vector bundle. Suppose it splits into a sum of non-negative, holomorphic line bundles and $\deg E < 3g-3$. Then $(X, E)$ will be a good model.
<!-- end prop-3 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
t suffices to show $h^0\big(X, \wedge^2\mathcal{E}\otimes T_X\big) = 0$. Let $X$ be a genus $g$ Riemann surface. Assu\-ming~$E$ is holomorphically split we can write $E = L_{d_1}\oplus L_{d_2}\oplus L_{d_3}$, for $L_{d_i}\rightarrow X$ a line bundle on~$X$ of degree~$d_i$. If $L_{d_i}$ is non-negative, then $d_i \geq 0$. Note that $\wedge^2E = L_{d_1+d_2} \oplus L_{d_1+d_3} \oplus L_{d_2+d_3}$; and $\deg \wedge^2E = 2\deg E = 2(d_1+d_2+d_3)$. With $\deg T_X = 2 - 2g$ and the above description of~$\wedge^2E$ we see that $h^0\big(\wedge^2\mathcal{E}\otimes T_X\big) = 0$ when
\begin{gather*}
d_1 + d_2 < 2g - 2, \qquad d_1 + d_3 < 2g - 2 \qquad \text{and}\qquad d_2 + d_3 < 2g - 2.
\end{gather*}
These conditions are equivalent to $\deg E < 3g-3$ when $d_i\geq 0$ for each $i$.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- thm-6: body_md -->
\label{rfh794hf984f98j}Let $E = L_{d_1}\oplus L_{d_2}\oplus L_{d_3}$ be a rank~$3$, holomorphic vector bundle on $\mathbb{P}^1_\mathbb{C}$, where~$L_{d_i}$ is a line bundle on~$\mathbb{P}^1_\mathbb{C}$ of degree~$d_i$. Then $(\mathbb{P}_{\mathbb{C}}^1, E)$ will be a good model if and only if at least one of~$d_i \neq -1$.
<!-- end thm-6 -->
<!-- lem-4: body_md -->
\label{rhf84h94h89484409}Let $E\rightarrow X$ be a rank $q$, holomorphic vector bundle. Any $(q-1)$-split atlas in $\check{H}^1\big(X, \mathcal{G}_{(X, E)}^{(q)}\big)$ in the image of a non-trivial section in $H^0\big(X, \mathcal{Q}^{(q-1)}_{(X, E)}\big)$ will be obstructed and hence, by Lemma~{\rm \ref{4hf84hf89hf8998f3j}}, exotic.
<!-- end lem-4 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
rite $\mathcal{E} = \mathcal{O}(d_1) \oplus\mathcal{O}(d_2)\oplus\mathcal{O}(d_3)$, where $\mathcal{E}$ denotes the sheaf of sections of $E$. Then
\begin{gather*}
\mathcal{Q}^{(2)}_{(\mathbb{P}^1_\mathbb{C}, E)}= \mathcal{O}(d_1 + d_2 + 2)\oplus \mathcal{O}(d_1 + d_3 + 2)\oplus\mathcal{O}(d_2 + d_3 + 2) \qquad \text{and}\\
\mathcal{Q}_{(\mathbb{P}^1_\mathbb{C}, E)}^{(3)}= \mathcal{O}(d_1 + d_2)\oplus \mathcal{O}(d_1 + d_3)\oplus\mathcal{O}(d_2 + d_3).
\end{gather*}
In order to construct an exotic atlas for a supermanifold modelled on $\big(\mathbb{P}^1_\mathbb{C}, E\big)$ it will be necessary for
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]\itemsep=0pt
	\item $h^0\big(\mathcal{Q}^{(2)}_{(\mathbb{P}^1_\mathbb{C}, E)} \big)\neq 0$ (by Proposition~\ref{tyhryg7hfiujfoiej} and Remark~\ref{rhf984hf89hf893h8}) and
	\item $h^1\big(\mathcal{Q}_{(\mathbb{P}^1_\mathbb{C}, E)}^{(3)}\big) \neq0$ (since $\mathcal{G}^{(3)}_{(\mathbb{P}^1_\mathbb{C}, E)}\cong \mathcal{Q}_{(\mathbb{P}^1_\mathbb{C}, E)}^{(3)}$ here).
\end{enumerate}
From Bott's formula on the dimension of the cohomology of line bundles on projective space,\footnote{See, e.g., \cite[p.~4]{OSS}.} both~(i) and~(ii) will be satisfied if and only if $(d_1, d_2, d_3) = (-1,-1, -1)$. Now in this case, where $(d_1, d_2, d_3) = (-1,-1, -1)$, we have by Serre duality
\begin{gather*}
 H^0\big(\mathbb{P}_\mathbb{C}^1, \mathcal{Q}^{(2)}_{(\mathbb{P}^1_\mathbb{C}, E)}\big)\cong H^1\big(\mathbb{P}_\mathbb{C}^1, \mathcal{Q}^{(3)}_{(\mathbb{P}^1_\mathbb{C}, E)}\big).
\end{gather*}
Upon observing $H^1\big(\mathbb{P}_\mathbb{C}^1, \mathcal{Q}^{(3)}_{(\mathbb{P}^1_\mathbb{C}, E)}\big)\cong \check{H}^1\big(\mathbb{P}^1_\mathbb{C}, \mathcal{G}^{(3)}_{(\mathbb{P}_\mathbb{C}^1, E)}\big)$, the theorem will then follow from Lem\-ma~\ref{rhf84h94h89484409} applied to $q = 3$.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- thm-7: body_md -->
\label{hf78hf984f8j40f094}Let $E\rightarrow \mathbb{P}^1_\mathbb{C}$ be a rank $q$, holomorphic vector bundle. Suppose $E = \oplus^qL_d$ where $L_d\rightarrow \mathbb{P}_\mathbb{C}^1$ is a line bundle of degree $d$. Then
\begin{enumerate}[$(i)$]\itemsep=0pt
	\item if $d = -1$ then $\big(\mathbb{P}^1_\mathbb{C}, E\big)$ will support exotic atlases;
	\item if $d < -1$, then $\big(\mathbb{P}^1_\mathbb{C}, E\big)$ will be a good model.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end thm-7 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
=-1 Let $\mathcal{O}(d)$ denote the sheaf of sections of $L_d$ so that $\mathcal{E} = \oplus^q\mathcal{O}(d)$. We begin by pro\-ving~(ii). We have generally $\wedge^k\mathcal{E} = \oplus^{\binom{q}{k}}\mathcal{O}(kd)$. As such the obstruction sheaves are given by
\begin{gather}
\mathcal{Q}_{(\mathbb{P}_\mathbb{C}^1, E)}^{(k)}=
\begin{cases}
\oplus^{\binom{q}{k}} \mathcal{O}(kd+2), &\text{$k$ is even},\\
\oplus^{k\binom{q}{k}}\mathcal{O}\big((k-1)d\big), &\text{$k$ is odd}.
\end{cases}\label{rfj984hf894jf90f903}
\end{gather}
Note that $2\leq k\leq q$ here. Evidently, if $d< -1$ the obstruction sheaves will be sums of line bundles of negative degree. Hence $H^0\big(\mathbb{P}_\mathbb{C}^1, \mathcal{Q}_{(\mathbb{P}_\mathbb{C}^1, E)}^{(k)}\big) = (0)$. Part (ii) then follows from Proposition~\ref{tyhryg7hfiujfoiej}. As for part~(i), firstly note that
\begin{align}
\wedge^\bullet \mathcal{E} &= \wedge^0\mathcal{E} \oplus \wedge^1\mathcal{E}\oplus \wedge^2\mathcal{E} \oplus\cdots\oplus \wedge^q\mathcal{E}\notag\\
&=\mathcal{O}(0)\oplus \big[\oplus^q\mathcal{O}(d)\big] \oplus\big[\oplus^{\binom{q}{2}}\mathcal{O}(2d)\big]\oplus \cdots \oplus \mathcal{O}(qd).
\notag
\end{align}
We have $\operatorname{{\mathcal A}ut} \mathcal{E}\!\subset\! \oplus^{q^2}\mathcal{O}(0)$ and $\operatorname{{\mathcal A}ut}\wedge^\bullet \mathcal{E}\!\subset\! \oplus_{0\leq a\leq b\leq q}\mathcal{O}((b-a)d)$. Note in particular that~\smash{$b-a\geq 0$}. Regarding the sheaf $\mathcal{G}_{(\mathbb{P}_\mathbb{C}^1, E)}^{(k)}$ observe that it can be realised as a subsheaf of $\oplus_{0\leq a< b\leq q}\mathcal{O}((b-a)d)$ where now $b-a \geq k-1$. Therefore if $d < 0$:
\begin{gather}
H^0\big(\mathbb{P}_\mathbb{C}^1, \mathcal{G}_{(\mathbb{P}_\mathbb{C}^1, E)}^{(k)}\big) = \{1\},\label{rfh784hfhf983jf9030}
\end{gather}
for all $k\geq 2$. Now if $d = -1$ then $h^0\big(\mathbb{P}^1_\mathbb{C}, \mathcal{Q}_{(\mathbb{P}_\mathbb{C}^1, E)}^{(2)}\big) =\binom{q}{2}\neq0$ from~\eqref{rfj984hf894jf90f903}. Since $H^0\big(\mathbb{P}_\mathbb{C}^1, \mathcal{G}_{(\mathbb{P}_\mathbb{C}^1, E)}^{(2)}\big) = \{e\}$ from~\eqref{rfh784hfhf983jf9030} we have the exact sequence
\begin{gather*}
\{1\}\longrightarrow H^0\big(\mathbb{P}^1_\mathbb{C}, \mathcal{Q}_{(\mathbb{P}_\mathbb{C}^1, E)}^{(2)}\big) \stackrel{\alpha}{\longrightarrow} \check{H}^1\big(\mathbb{P}^1_\mathbb{C}, \mathcal{G}_{(\mathbb{P}_\mathbb{C}^1, E)}^{(3)}\big),
\end{gather*}
where $\alpha$ is the boundary map from~\eqref{jghhthrjdkfhnrjeo8474}. In particular $\alpha$ does not vanish and any atlas in its image will be exotic.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- prop-4: body_md -->
\label{rhf98hf74hf984fj039}Let $C$ be a Riemann surface of genus one and $E\rightarrow C$ a holomorphic, rank~$3$ vector bundle. Then $(C, E)$ will be a good model when either:
\begin{enumerate}[$(i)$]\itemsep=0pt
	\item $\deg \mathcal{Q}_{(C, E)}^{(2)} = h^0\big(\mathcal{Q}_{(C, E)}^{(2)}\big)$ or
	\item $\deg \mathcal{Q}_{(C, E)}^{(2)} = -h^1\big(\mathcal{Q}_{(C, E)}^{(2)}\big)$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end prop-4 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
n genus one note that $T_C = \mathcal{O}_C$ is a line bundle of degree zero. Hence we have a~natural isomorphism $\mathcal{Q}_{(C, E)}^{(2)} \cong \mathcal{Q}_{(C, E)}^{(3)}$. The proposition now follows from the Riemann--Roch theorem.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
et $\mathfrak{X}$ be a supermanifold modelled on~$(X, E)$ and suppose its primary obstruction~$\omega_*(\mathfrak{X})$ does not vanish. The map~$\omega_*\colon \check{H}^1\big(X, \mathcal{G}^{(2)}_{(X, E)}\big) \rightarrow H^1\big(X, \mathcal{Q}_{(X, E)}^{(2)}\big)$ is a map of pointed sets, sending the basepoint $\{e\}\in \check{H}^1\big(X, \mathcal{G}^{(2)}_{(X, E)}\big)$ to the basepoint $0\in H^1\big(X, \mathcal{Q}_{(X, E)}^{(2)}\big)$. Since $\omega_*(\mathfrak{X}) \neq 0$, $\mathfrak{X}$ cannot be split.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- prop-5: body_md -->
\label{rfg784gf98hf89j3f03}The composition of maps $\omega_*\delta$ in \eqref{rfh74hf983jfj30} vanishes.
<!-- end prop-5 -->
<!-- lem-5: body_md -->
\label{rfu4f9h38f03jf93jf93j}Let $(X, E)$ be a model. The subgroup $\mathbb{C}^\times\cdot 1_E< \operatorname{Aut}(E)$ acts on the $k$-th obstruction space $H^1\big(X, \mathcal{Q}_{(X, E)}^{(k)}\big)$ by sending $v \mapsto \lambda^kv$ for any vector $v\in H^1\big(X, \mathcal{Q}_{(X, E)}^{(k)}\big)$.
<!-- end lem-5 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
From Theorem~\ref{groeiveytvdbno} we know that $\operatorname{Aut}(E)$ will act on $\check{H}^1\big(X, \mathcal{G}^{(2)}_{(X, E)}\big)$. Denote this action by $\star$. Our first claim is that the subgroup $\mathbb{C}^\times\cdot 1_E$ will act trivially on the image of $\operatorname{Aut}(E)$. To see this, let $(U_i\rightarrow X)$ be an open cover and $\phi \in \operatorname{Aut}(E)$. If $\widetilde\phi_i\in \big(\operatorname{{\mathcal A}ut}\wedge^\bullet\mathcal{E}\big)(U_i)$ are local lifts of $\phi_i$, then
\begin{gather*}
\delta(\phi)_{ij}= \widetilde\phi_i \widetilde\phi_j^{-1}.
\end{gather*}
Now clearly any $\lambda\cdot 1_E\in \mathbb{C}^\times \cdot 1_E< \operatorname{Aut}(E)$ will act by sending $\phi_i \mapsto \lambda \phi_i$. Hence,
\begin{gather}
\big(\lambda\cdot 1_E\big)\star \delta(\phi)_{ij} = \big(\lambda \widetilde\phi_i\big)\big(\lambda^{-1}\widetilde\phi_j^{-1}\big) =\widetilde\phi_i \widetilde\phi_j^{-1}=\delta(\phi)_{ij}.\label{rhf894hf8h09fj30jf930}
\end{gather}
The group $\operatorname{Aut}(E)$ will act on $\check{H}^1\big(X, \mathcal{G}^{(2)}_{(X, E)}\big)$ and this action will induce an action on $H^1\big(X, \mathcal{Q}_{(X, E)}^{(2)}\big)$. The action of $\mathbb{C}^\times\cdot 1_E$ mentioned in Lemma~\ref{rfu4f9h38f03jf93jf93j} is compatible with this in\-du\-ced $\operatorname{Aut}(E)$ action. In particular we can conclude: for a supermanifold $\mathfrak{X}\in \check{H}^1\big(X, \mathcal{G}^{(2)}_{(X, E)}\big)$ and any $\lambda\cdot 1_E\in \mathbb{C}^\times\cdot1_E$,
\begin{gather}
\omega_*\big((\lambda\cdot 1_E)\star \mathfrak{X}\big)=\lambda^2\omega_*\big(\mathfrak{X}\big).\label{rhf893h8j30fj390}
\end{gather}
In comparing \eqref{rhf894hf8h09fj30jf930} and \eqref{rhf893h8j30fj390} we see that if $\mathfrak{X} = \delta(\phi)$, we must have $\omega_*\big(\mathfrak{X}\big) = 0$. This proves Proposition~\ref{rfg784gf98hf89j3f03} from whence Theorem~\ref{4fh984fj8jf093j303kf} follows.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
